---
title: "Install & set up"
description: "Everything you need on your computer to run the examples: R, Python, Git, Positron, and this repository."
---

This takes 30–45 minutes the first time, and you only do it once per computer. Follow the steps in order. Steps 1 to 3 and 5 to 7 end with a quick check, and step 8 checks everything at the end.

::: {.callout-note}
## 💡 In plain language
**R** and **Python** are the programming languages that do the statistics. **Positron** is the app you type code into. **Git** downloads this repository (a folder of code and data) and keeps track of changes. **uv** installs Python and its add-on packages. The **terminal** is a window where you type commands: **Terminal** on a Mac (press Cmd+Space, type "Terminal" and press Return), **PowerShell** on Windows (open the Start menu, type "PowerShell" and press Enter).
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Just want to read?
You don't need to install anything to read this site. Install only when you're ready to run code yourself.
:::

## 1. Install R {#install-r}

1. Go to <https://cloud.r-project.org>.
2. Click **Download R for macOS** or **Download R for Windows**.
   - **Mac:** pick the installer for your chip. Apple menu → **About This Mac**: "Apple M…" means *Apple silicon (arm64)*, and "Intel" means *Intel (x86_64)*.
   - **Windows:** click **base**, then the download link at the top of the page.
3. Open the downloaded file and accept the defaults.

**Check:** you will see R in Positron's language picker in step 6. On a Mac you can also open Terminal and type `R --version`.

## 2. Install uv and Python {#install-uv-and-python}

**Mac:** open Terminal and run:

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

**Windows:** open PowerShell and run:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
```

Close the window, open a new one, and install Python:

```bash
uv python install 3.13
```

**Check:** `uv --version` prints a version number.

## 3. Install Git {#install-git}

- **Mac:** in Terminal, run `xcode-select --install` and click **Install**. This installs Apple's command-line tools, which include Git.
- **Windows:** download Git from <https://git-scm.com/downloads> and accept the defaults. At HFR, when the installer asks where to install Git, make sure the folder is on `C:`, not on a network drive such as `K:`.

**Check:** `git --version` prints a version number.

## 4. Install Positron {#install-positron}

Download Positron from <https://positron.posit.co> and install it like any other app. Positron runs R and Python side by side. Prefer RStudio or VS Code? See [Other editors](#other-editors).

## 5. Get this repository {#get-this-repository}

In Terminal (Mac) or PowerShell (Windows), make a `projects` folder and download ("clone") the repository into it:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/projects
cd ~/projects
git clone https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation.git
```

Use a folder that is **not** synced to the cloud. `Documents` and `Desktop` are often synced by iCloud (Mac) or OneDrive (Windows). Syncing slows down, and can break, the R and Python environments that steps 6 and 7 create.

Then, in Positron: **File → Open Folder…** and choose `stats-formation`.

**Check:** `git clone` starts with `Cloning into 'stats-formation'...` and prints no line that starts with `fatal`. If it prints one, look for it under [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting). In Positron, the file list on the left (click the Explorer icon if you don't see it) shows the repository's folders, among them `data` and `scripts`.

## 6. Install the R packages {#install-the-r-packages}

In Positron, start an R console: use the language picker at the top right of the **Console** pane and choose **R**. Because R starts inside the repository folder, it switches on this project's package list. Then run:

```r
renv::restore()
```

Answer **Y** if asked. This installs every R package the tutorials use, at the exact versions we tested. It takes a few minutes.

**Check:** the output ends without a line that starts with `Error`. To be sure, run `renv::status()` in the same console: it answers `No issues found -- the project is in a consistent state.` When R starts in this folder for the first time, it may print `Bootstrapping renv` and `One or more packages recorded in the lockfile are not installed.` Both are expected before `renv::restore()` has run.

## 7. Install the Python packages {#install-the-python-packages}

Open Positron's terminal (**Terminal → New Terminal**). It opens in the repository folder. Run:

```bash
uv sync
```

This creates a private Python environment in the `.venv` folder with every package the tutorials use. Then tell Positron to use it: in the **Console** pane's language picker, choose the Python whose path includes `.venv`.

**Check:** the first time, `uv sync` prints `Creating virtual environment at: .venv`, then one line for each package it installed, starting with `+`. No line starts with `error`.

## 8. Check that everything works {#check-that-everything-works}

In Positron's terminal, run both checks:

```bash
Rscript scripts/check_setup.R
uv run python scripts/check_setup.py
```

Each check ends with `All good - you are ready.` If a line says `PROBLEM`, it tells you what to do. Fix it and run the check again.

On Windows, if `Rscript` is "not recognized", run the R check from Positron's R console instead:

```r
source("scripts/check_setup.R")
```

## Reading the data without cloning {#reading-the-data-without-cloning}

You can skip steps 5 to 8 and read the practice data straight from GitHub, for example to use it in a project of your own. You still need R (step 1) or uv and Python (step 2), and the packages below.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
install.packages(c("readr", "readxl"))   # once

cohort <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/main/data/cohort.csv")
```

## Python

Start Python with the packages it needs. In a terminal:

```bash
uv run --with pandas --with openpyxl python
```

Then:

```python
import pandas as pd

cohort = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/main/data/cohort.csv")
```
:::

Every CSV works the same way: replace `"data/"` with `"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/main/data/"`. To run a whole example from a tutorial page, clone the repository instead (steps 5 to 7): the pages use many more packages than these, and cloning installs them all at the versions we tested.

Excel files are different. R's `read_excel()` can't read a web address, so download the file first. Python's `pd.read_excel()` can read the address directly.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/main/data/messy_abstraction_workbook.xlsx"
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
download.file(url, path, mode = "wb")   # "wb" keeps the file intact on Windows
site_a <- readxl::read_excel(path, sheet = "Site A")
```

## Python

```python
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/main/data/messy_abstraction_workbook.xlsx"
site_a = pd.read_excel(url, sheet_name="Site A")
```
:::

### Every data file {#data-files}

Each link below gets one file. An Excel file downloads. A CSV file opens as text in your browser: to save it, right-click the link and choose the command that saves the linked file. Every file is synthetic, like all the data on this site.

Each tidy dataset has a codebook that lists its columns: what each one means, its type, its units and the values it may hold. A codebook link opens on GitHub, which shows the codebook as a table.

| File | One row per | Codebook |
|------|------|------|
| [`data/cohort.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/cohort.csv) | case (one primary hip or knee replacement) | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/cohort.csv) |
| [`data/proms_long.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/proms_long.csv) | case and visit | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/proms_long.csv) |
| [`data/matched_sets.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/matched_sets.csv) | case in a matched set of three | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/matched_sets.csv) |
| [`data/radiographic_reliability.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/radiographic_reliability.csv) | knee, rater and session | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/radiographic_reliability.csv) |
| [`data/hip_fracture.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/hip_fracture.csv) | patient aged 65 or over with a hip fracture | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/hip_fracture.csv) |
| [`data/foot_ankle_rct.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/foot_ankle_rct.csv) | randomized patient | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/foot_ankle_rct.csv) |
| [`data/foot_ankle_rct_long.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/foot_ankle_rct_long.csv) | randomized patient and visit | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/foot_ankle_rct_long.csv) |
| [`data/acl_cohort.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/acl_cohort.csv) | primary ACL reconstruction | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/acl_cohort.csv) |
| [`data/hip_preservation_imaging.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/hip_preservation_imaging.csv) | hip | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/hip_preservation_imaging.csv) |

Two files are messy on purpose. [Tidy data](../foundations/01-tidy-data.qmd) puts them in order, and each has an answer key: the tidy result it should become.

| Messy file | Where it is tidied | Answer key | Codebook of the answer key |
|------|------|------|------|
| [`data/messy_abstraction_workbook.xlsx`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/messy_abstraction_workbook.xlsx) | [Tidying a messy workbook](../foundations/01-tidy-data.qmd#tidying) | [`data/answer-keys/abstraction_workbook_tidy.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/answer-keys/abstraction_workbook_tidy.csv) | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/abstraction_workbook_tidy.csv) |
| [`data/messy_survey_export.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/messy_survey_export.csv) | [Reshaping a survey export](../foundations/01-tidy-data.qmd#reshaping) | [`data/answer-keys/survey_items_long.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/answer-keys/survey_items_long.csv) | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/survey_items_long.csv) |

The data collection template that [Tidy data](../foundations/01-tidy-data.qmd#collecting) describes is [`templates/data-collection-template.xlsx`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/templates/data-collection-template.xlsx).

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

| You see | Do this |
|------|------|
| `You have not agreed to the Xcode license` (Mac, during `renv::restore()`) | In Terminal, run `sudo xcodebuild -license accept` and type your Mac password. Then run `renv::restore()` again. |
| `there is no package called 'renv'` | In the R console, run `install.packages("renv")`. Restart R (**Session → Restart R**) and run `renv::restore()` again. |
| `uv: command not found`, or "not recognized" | Close the terminal window, open a new one, and try again. |
| `git: command not found` | Repeat step 3. |
| `Could not resolve host: github.com` (in the `fatal` line after `git clone`) | Git couldn't look up where `github.com` is, so it downloaded nothing. The command you typed isn't the cause. At HFR this happens when Git is installed on a network drive, such as `K:`: Git has to be on the computer's own disk. To see where it is, run `where.exe git` in PowerShell. If the answer starts with `K:` or another network drive, uninstall Git and install it again (step 3) in a folder on `C:`. If the computer doesn't let you, do the setup on an HFR laptop or on your own computer. Your own computer is fine for this site's practice data, which is synthetic; real study data stays where [Where HFR data lives](real-data.qmd#where) says. |
| Python can't find `pandas` in Positron | Choose the `.venv` Python in the Console language picker (step 7), then restart the console. |
| Anything else | Copy the whole error message and send it to your project lead. |

## Other editors {#other-editors}

- **RStudio** (<https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>) is great for R. It can run Python too, but Positron is simpler when you use both.
- **VS Code** (<https://code.visualstudio.com>) works too: install the R and Python extensions.

Everything else on this page stays the same.
